newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil cargoes flat but barges volatile.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil cargoes flat but barges volatile.

text.p: NWE high sulphur fuel oil barges changed hands at widely differing numbers again on Friday but cargoes were little changed, traders said.

High sulphur barges traded in the morning at $91.50 and $92 fob ARA but then the week's main buyer stepped in to pick up product at $97, $98 and $99 traders said. A Shell trader said he expected production at the Rotterdam refinery to return to normal production "after the weekend".
High sulphur cargoes were little changed and while storage supply remains ample, refinery barrels were not actively heard offered.

A Scottish utility was heard to have bought a high sulphur cargo from an ARA player on Thursday at $98.50 cif NWE. Dealers said this was above the market because of the restrictive quality specifications required. Other utility players were not expected to pay more than around $92/$92 cif NWE.
Another ARA player was also heard to have bought an M-100 cargo out of Tallinn, sailing on the Mars, at $98 cif ARA.
Low sulphur fuel oil was again unchanged in thin markets.
Dealers said they thought fixed price indications were somewhere around February swaps levels, which themselves were pegged at $103/$104 fob NWE.
